name: Diyi Yang
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
lab_name: Stanford Social and Language Technologies (SALT) Lab
research_topics: Large Language Models (LLMs) and Human-AI Interaction
Generative interfaces and generative user modeling
Large audio / speech models and their evaluation
AI, culture and society; dialects and low-resource contexts
current_direction: Auditing what AI agents actually do to human work (automation vs. augmentation across occupations)
LLM agents that autonomously ideate and execute research, judged on execution outcomes rather than proposals
Generative interfaces and user modeling that let LLMs adapt the UI to the person
Open audio/speech foundation models plus benchmarks for evaluating them
Human wellbeing and community-centered auditing: AI companions, sycophancy, whose knowledge counts
current_direction_basis: Driven by the 2025-2026 items collected here: 'Future of Work with AI Agents' (arXiv 2506.06576) and 'How Do AI Agents Do Human Work?' (arXiv 2510.22780) for the work/agent auditing thread; 'The Ideation-Execution Gap' (ICLR 2026) and 'Towards Execution-Grounded Automated AI Research' (ICML 2026) for autonomous-research agents; 'Generative Interfaces for Language Models' (arXiv 2508.19227) plus the homepage's 'Generative Interaction: Generative UI, Generative User Modeling (GUM)' project list for generative interfaces; 'Scaling Open Discrete Audio Foundation Models' (arXiv 2602.16687, submitted 18 Feb 2026) and 'AudioJudge' (arXiv 2507.12705) for the audio thread; 'Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being' (Nature Human Behaviour, Aug 2026), 'Whose Knowledge Counts?' (CHI 2026) and 'Verbalizing LLMs' Assumptions About the User ... Reduce Sycophancy' (CHI 2026) for the wellbeing/auditing thread. The SALT lab news line for 1/2026 ('actively making progress on both the AI and HCI side of human-centered AI') corroborates the split.
